claim: The printing press invented by Gutenberg around 1440 democratized access to information and accelerated the spread of ideas across Europe
Media literacy is the ability to critically analyze and evaluate media messages including identifying bias misinformation and propaganda techniques
The attention economy describes competition for human attention as a scarce resource in an information-rich world
Filter bubbles occur when algorithms personalize content so users primarily see information that reinforces existing beliefs
The Streisand effect describes how attempts to suppress information online often increase its visibility
Misinformation spreads faster and farther than accurate information on social media platforms according to multiple studies
Fact-checking organizations verify claims against evidence and rate them on accuracy scales helping combat misinformation
Net neutrality is the principle that internet service providers must treat all data equally without discriminating by user site or content
Deepfake technology uses AI to create realistic fake video and audio content raising concerns about trust and authentication
Public interest journalism serves as a watchdog on power holding governments and institutions accountable through investigative reporting
Digital preservation ensures that electronic records and cultural heritage remain accessible as technology formats become obsolete
The right to be forgotten allows individuals to request removal of personal information from search engines and databases under certain conditions
